- Keep crawler running actively
  - Check the Observability and Metrics
  - Geonode mbps >=100mbps always
  - (when p1, p2,p4 is achieved, withinnitial stability 6h+ check, they now should come to duty.)
  - instagram profiles at 10k+/min,
  - nothing is backlogging: pg -> os/ch, media worker, (... idk you know better.)
  - ...
  - when p6 is achieved, it is your duty to keep LGTM and Grafana dashbaords up to date to any changes, and carefully tune the alerts system. if it's false alert -> try to reduce it change condition. if alert missed it (wasn't in place) but found actually meaningful issue, add that alert so we don't have to worry about it. (10-19, msg mvfe8foz)
goal: Every crawl with a throughput goal crawls at or above it on prod, read the way the crawler Throughput dashboard on obs.virev.ai shows it. The duty moved from Crawler VP's d9 to Crawler guy's d8 on 11-24 (owner, t9). The hand-over moved open steps only, so the goals that closed on Crawler VP's board stay this duty's own lines in throughput-goal.ts: Instagram profiles at 10,000 good a minute held 6 h (Crawler VP's p826, owner 10-19 p1), TikTok Shop products at 99.5% or more of live US products with an ok read in the last 7 days, gone products left out (Crawler ops 10-23), and Meta Ads advertiser re-reads with every due advertiser read within 7 days (Crawler VP's p850). Instagram re-reads read their goal from Crawler guy's board item p8 at run time, its target or the number in its title (owner 10-26 "1k+ every month, 10K+ every week" and "under 1k also monthly"): at most that share of read accounts with 10,000+ followers past 7 days, and of the rest past 30 days, two rows from page samples of instagram_census. The headline counts the goals prod misses. Instagram reads the slowest rolling hour of the last 6 h, the dashboard's "slowest hour, 6 h" stats, with the 5-minute slots under prod's deploy lock left out (deploy downtime is p6's number): Instagram counts instagram_account_snapshots, every profile read on any path, and TikTok Shop its good product reads; Meta Ads reads advertiser walks finished over 24 h against the walks due now spread over 7 days. Crawls with no goal (TikTok and YouTube profiles, Instagram posts) are listed in the run detail and left out of the count. The census Postgres writer (Crawler VP's p895) is one more goal row: its worst lag over 24 h, in the 5-minute slots where Instagram profiles read 10,000 a minute or more outside deploys, stays at most 5,000 records, and a 24 h with no such slot reads 0 since the Instagram profiles row is that miss. The supporting metrics keep the rest of the owner's 10-19 duties: no Instagram queue backlogs, which is a 30-minute low over 80k records or growth over 6 h (p827), and every panel on the crawler dashboards draws. The GeoNode Mbps metric left this duty on 11-24: its 100 Mbps an hour floor is about 32 TB a month, against the 250 GB plan the owner bought that day, and Search product, misc.'s d4 watches the plan's use. GeoNode retries and connections stay with the GeoNode proxy use duty, read cost per profile with the Crawler read cost duty, Meta walk age with the Meta Ads crawl duty, and alert rules with the Crawler alerts duty. The census job failure share is reported in the run detail against the owner's 40 to 70% band, and a rise past it is an alert rule's job.

metrics.label: Throughput goals that prod misses, every platform
Instagram queues that backlog: over 80k at their 30-minute low, or grown over 6 h
Panels on the crawler dashboards on obs.virev.ai that show an error or No data

onMiss: For each missed metric, start or steer one live fix job this run, and keep it until the metric is met again. A live job that already owns the cause gets the numbers by message. Otherwise start one and put its fix step under the matching goal with duty "<id>/<metric>": the Instagram re-read rows go under p8, every other row under p6. throughput_goals_missed: the goal lines name each platform's rate against its goal; for each missed one find what stopped or slowed that crawl (a pause, a deploy, a hold, the proxy, a crashed role, a writer, a cadence control such as weekly_days or small_recheck_days) from the Throughput dashboard and logs, and get it back with a code or config fix through the crawler ops train, or a control write through /ops/controls with a measured reason. Keep each lane inside the 250 GB GeoNode month by sizing the work, never with a coded cap (c239). The census Postgres writer row: its line names the worst slot; read the census writer lane's process count (crawler_v3_runtime_role_processes{role="instagram-census-writer"}) and the lane scaler's last pass (crawler_v3_lane_scaler_last_pass_timestamp_seconds), then fix the writer or its scaler through the crawler ops train, never by holding the census rate down. ig_queues_growing_6h: name the queue and its consumer from the backlog line and fix the consumer. crawler_panels_blank: the dashboards line names each blank panel; fix its query in auto-sns-agent apps/infra/grafana/dashboards/crawler or the exporter it reads, or delete a panel nobody needs, and land it through the crawler ops train. A source_error comes first: fix the precheck read. The duty job itself only reads prod. All on target: end the turn with no message.
